finding: Grok's headless output carries NO tool events. It will run a command and describe the result in prose without ever announcing the call — verified at 0.2.111 by granting read tools, asking it to read a planted file, and seeing it report the file's contents with num_turns=2 and only text and thought in the stream. Four of the eight events are therefore all that can honestly be produced; the surface shows less rather than showing something invented.
quirks: `--allow` takes ONE rule per flag and rejects a space-separated list (`unknown tool prefix: …`). Use `--tools`, which takes a comma-separated list of built-in tool names.
Grok's tool names are its own: read_file, list_dir, grep, run_terminal_command, ask_user_question, spawn_subagent, … — not the names any other provider uses.
`run_terminal_command` cannot be scoped to a command prefix the way other providers scope a shell tool, so it is deliberately not granted.

`--permission-mode dontAsk` is ACCEPTED AND IGNORED: the session keeps the default prompting policy, and headless a call that would prompt is cancelled. Granting full access with it left the agent unable to write or run anything, explaining the refusal in prose while the turn reported success. Only `bypassPermissions` and `default` are applied by this flag; `dontAsk` must come from `defaultMode` in a settings file instead.

`--sandbox <profile>` is a NO-OP headless. Under `strict`, documented as reads limited to the working directory, it read a planted file well outside it, and under `read-only` it created a file both through `create_file` and through a shell redirect. The tool list is the only thing that actually scopes this CLI.
`--rules` appends to the system prompt (what we want); `--system-prompt-override` replaces it.
`--session-id` names a NEW conversation and refuses an id that already exists, so the resume handle can be minted before the first byte, as with Claude. Resume is `--resume <id>`.
`usage.input_tokens` excludes `cache_read_input_tokens` (they sum with output to total_tokens), so the split matches Claude's rather than Codex's.

vocabulary.why: reasoning text, streamed a token at a time — the only sign this brain gives that a turn is in progress, since it reports no tool work at all
the live stream — data is the chunk
sessionId is the resume handle; usage.input/output/cache_read map straight across; the first key of modelUsage is the model that answered; turn_done.ok = stopReason === 'EndTurn'
tool_call, tool_result, todo_update and clarify_request have no source in this CLI
